record.original_question: Let f(x_1,...,x_n) be a complex polynomial such that all moments M_m = integral_[0,1]^n f(x_1,...,x_n)^m dx_1...dx_n vanish for every m >= 1. Must f be identically zero?

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Let f(x1, x2, ..., xn) be a polynomial in C[x1, x2, ..., xn] such that the following moment conditions hold Mm := integral ... f^m(...) = 0, m >= 1. Is it true that f = 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ be an integer and let $f\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n]$ be a polynomial in $n$ variables with complex coefficients. For each integer $m\ge 1$, define the moment
$$M_m(f)\;=\;\int_{[0,1]^n} f(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n)^{\,m}\,dx_1\,dx_2\cdots dx_n.$$
Suppose that $M_m(f)=0$ for every integer $m\ge 1$. Must $f$ be identically zero?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on the polynomial moment problem (notably Muzychuk–Pakovich's solution of the one-dimensional Wronski-type polynomial moment problem and subsequent work on Laurent polynomial moment problems) did not turn up a published resolution of the multidimensional version on the unit cube $[0,1]^n$ asking whether vanishing of all moments $M_m=\int_{[0,1]^n} f^m$ forces $f\equiv 0$. The status of the multivariate problem appears to be unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Solution of the polynomial moment problem
status_evidence.snippet: Muzychuk and Pakovich solve the one-dimensional polynomial moment problem; the cited results address integrals over an interval rather than the unit cube in several variables.
status_evidence.claim: Existing solutions of the polynomial moment problem treat the one-dimensional case; no multivariate analogue on $[0,1]^n$ is provided.

status_evidence.title: Fedor Pakovich — publications
status_evidence.snippet: List of publications on the polynomial and Laurent polynomial moment problems, focused on one-variable settings.
status_evidence.claim: No paper in this body of work resolves the multivariate version of the problem.
